Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance criteria — draft attached

Samir / Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a working draft of a MAP that pairs milestones with measurable acceptance tests and a suggested 3-week pilot timeline. High level notes:

1) Acceptance checklist (summary) — pass if ALL items met:
   - Functional: model responses meet 85% intent-match on 1k sample prompts (detailed script in attachment)
   - Performance: p95 latency <= 450ms for 512-token generation under 50 RPS sustained; tokens/sec baseline captured via our synthetic harness
   - Reliability: no more than 2 transient errors / 10k requests during pilot; automatic fallback to smaller compatible variant on degradation
   - Security & compliance: access logging enabled to BlueBridge S3+Audit, SOC2 evidence folder delivered within 48 hours of request

2) Exit gates and rollback triggers:
   - Fail if functional fails on >15% of evaluation prompts after two remediation iterations
   - Fail if performance SLA breach persists beyond a 24-hour mitigation window and impacts >20% of test traffic

3) Test harness & artifacts:
   - Attached: acceptance-tests-catalog.pdf (defines probes, scoring, and sampling methodology)
   - Measurement: we’ll run side-by-side traffic replay + seeded live probes; results posted to shared Drive folder hourly

4) Timeline (suggested):
   - Week 0 (prep): MAP sign-off + contract terms, infra provisioning
   - Week 1 (ingestion & baseline): run baseline tests and small-sample validation
   - Week 2 (stress & edge): load tests, edge-case evaluation, security review
   - Week 3 (final validation & sign-off): run full acceptance suite; final sign-off meeting and cutover runway

I’ve attached three artifacts: BlueBridge_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action spreadsheet), acceptance-tests-catalog.pdf, and security-evidence-summary.pdf.

Quick ask for BlueBridge: can procurement confirm if a one-week mandatory procurement review (DocuSign + legal) exists on your side and whether there are any blackout dates in February? That impacts our cutover runway.

Laura / Tessa — heads up, I’m sharing the draft with the customer. Please review sections labelled [INTERNAL] in the MAP and weigh in on the remediation cadence and rollback policy.

Thanks — I’ll be available for a quick sync this afternoon if useful.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Team —

Copy of the customer-facing draft above. Key sections need your input before I finalize:

- Functional threshold: proposing 85% intent-match on 1k prompts (scored by deterministic rubric). Laura — can you confirm the rubric and whether 1k is sufficient sample size for BlueBridge's use case?
- Performance threshold: p95 <= 450ms @ 50 RPS sustained. Tessa — is that realistic on our dedicated pool with quantized variant? If not, propose target and fallback model variant timing.
- Remediation cadence: propose two remediation iterations (48–72h each) before gating to fail. Marissa — sales ask: would BlueBridge accept a single 5% credit if we need an extra remediation window?

Please reply with line edits in the spreadsheet (BlueBridge_MAP_v1.xlsx) or comments in the Drive doc. I’ll incorporate and send final by EOD.

Vivek

Subject: Re: MAP + acceptance criteria — two procurement notes

Vivek —

Thanks for the thoughtful draft. A couple of procurement and product notes:

1) Procurement: We have a standard 7-business-day legal review for pilots that include data access clauses. Can you confirm Redwood’s standard pilot contract vs an enterprise contract redline? We may need a faster evidence package for legal to expedite.

2) Product: 85% intent-match is acceptable as a starting bar, but we need the rubric to be deterministic and shared. We will also include a small hand-labeled set (200 prompts) from our domain to seed the evaluation. Can Redwood run the seeded set and include it in the acceptance pass/fail calculation?

3) Minor redline: remove the proposed 5% credit remediation clause — procurement prefers fixed remediation windows (two iterations) with rollback to previous model rather than credits.

If you can confirm: (A) that seeded set is supported, (B) SOC2 evidence can be provided within 48 hours of request, and (C) a 3-week pilot still fits legal’s review window (with procurement's 7 business days), we’ll lock in the kickoff on Feb 23 and aim for cutover March 16 (approx).

Best,

Elena / Samir —

Thanks for the clarity. Confirming items and next steps:

A) Seeded set: confirmed — Redwood will ingest BlueBridge’s 200 hand-labeled prompts and include those results in the final pass/fail calculation. We’ll provide the scoring script and rubrics (deterministic) in the shared Drive by Feb 20.

B) SOC2 evidence: we’ll share the summary package (security-evidence-summary.pdf) within 24–48 hours of your formal request; full artifacts can be shared under the NDA/legal channel.

C) Procurement timeline: we acknowledge the 7-business-day review. Suggested kickoff: Feb 23 (prep week), pilot window Feb 29–Mar 20 (3 weeks of validation, with weekend buffer). Final sign-off meeting provisionally set for Mar 23.

D) Acceptance tests (finalized):
   - Functional: >= 85% combined pass rate across seeded 200 + 800 sampled prompts (detailed in acceptance-tests-catalog.pdf)
   - Performance: p95 <= 450ms measured via Redwood harness on the dedicated pool; results aggregated hourly and shared to the Drive
   - Reliability: automated health checks, and fallback policy engaged if error rate >0.02% sustained over 1 hour

E) Exit gates & rollback: failure after two remediation iterations (48h each) will trigger rollback to the prior model variant; no credits will be issued per customer's preference.

Next steps:
- Vivek: finalize rubrics + update MAP spreadsheet (I’ll attach a final copy to Drive by Feb 20)
- BlueBridge: confirm kickoff Feb 23 and share the 200 seeded prompts by Feb 20
- Procurement: confirm DocuSign contact for pilot amendment

If that all looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff invite for Feb 23 and include the acceptance-runbook as an agenda item.
